data.name: FindThis_Griffin_BaseUrl_Title
data.value: How to Find Your Griffin Base URL

data.name: FindThis_Griffin_BaseUrl_Step1_Desc
data.value: Log in to your Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS) admin portal using your administrator credentials.

data.name: FindThis_Griffin_BaseUrl_Step2_Desc
data.value: In the ADFS console, expand your server name and click on "Service" → "Federation Service Properties". Look for the "Federation Service identifier" field.

data.name: FindThis_Griffin_BaseUrl_Step3_Desc
data.value: The Federation Service identifier is your Griffin Base URL. It typically follows this format:

data.name: FindThis_Griffin_BaseUrl_Note
data.value: The URL should use HTTP or HTTPS protocol. If you cannot access the ADFS console, contact your IT administrator for the correct Federation Service URL.

data.name: FindThis_Email_ApiKey_Title
data.value: How to Find Your Email API Key

data.name: FindThis_Email_ApiKey_Step1_Title
data.value: Log In to Your Email Service Provider

data.name: FindThis_Email_ApiKey_Step1_Desc
data.value: Access your email service provider's admin dashboard or developer console (e.g., SendGrid, Mailgun, AWS SES, etc.).

data.name: FindThis_Email_ApiKey_Step2_Desc
data.value: Look for "API Keys", "API Credentials", or "Developer Settings" in your account menu. This is usually found under Settings, Account, or API sections.

data.name: FindThis_Email_ApiKey_Step3_Desc
data.value: If you don't have an API key yet, click "Create API Key" or "Generate New Key". Make sure to grant it permission to send emails. Copy the key immediately as some providers only show it once.

data.name: FindThis_Email_ApiKey_SecurityNote
data.value: Never share your API key publicly or commit it to version control. Store it securely and rotate it periodically for enhanced security.
